cells.tense: The pull is on you now, and the options are spread out where you can see them.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take the strongest pull and follow what comes after it, step by step, to the end — where it lands, what it costs, what it gives. Do the figuring first, then feel.
cells.core:
Feelings gather themselves before you decide — the pull of what might be felt between you and someone. From here it comes apart into a clear line, and what you're holding is a set of paths, each one readable to the end before you walk it.

That's the good face, and it's the one to keep. While the options are still open, take the strongest pull and trace it to its end — where it lands, what it costs, what it gives — before you touch the feeling side of it. The rest go quiet on their own once the line is drawn, and what's left with you is a real choice instead of a fog.
cells.sheetLine: The pull has a logic. Run it before you trust it.
cells.verb: gathering every possible feeling into one cloud of choice
cells.place: down where the tangled thing thins into a clean line

cells.tense: By the time anything arrives, you'll already have lived every version of it.
cells.ask: Pick the option that exists outside your head — the person you could ring tonight — and stay with that one all week. Leave the rest of the cloud alone.
cells.core:
The pull of what might be felt is running ahead. You feel out a possibility, and then another one, and the first is already a season old in your head. Being wanted reads like a mechanism, connection like a formula, and what's actually moving — somebody, a real feeling that is still live — arrives second-hand, opposed by what you've already lived.

The pattern has its own pull, and it gets stronger the longer you look. So pick the option that exists outside your own head, the person you could ring tonight, and give your attention only there this week. Let the rest sit. The pattern folds itself back onto the actual, and the person across the table becomes the one you're reading instead of one of the options.
cells.sheetLine: You're meeting tomorrow before it happens.

cells.tense: One possibility was real, and you're at the part where it was open.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: For one stretch, don't work the problem at all — no weighing, no replays. A walk, a job under your hand, anything that asks nothing of the mind. Then stop.
cells.core:
The options came, and none of them carried you out. The pull of what might be felt is worn thin now — you can see the shape of what didn't happen, but not a line out of it. From the outside you weren't wrong about it; the whole thing is just older than tonight, and you're sorting what it meant.

So stop working the problem for one stretch. A walk, something under your hand, nothing that asks you to figure anything out. The turns it took don't want the answer again. You come back to the one who is here and not back at the doorway, and from there the next possibility can land.
cells.sheetLine: A door closed and you're still at its frame.

cells.tense: The feelings are being read as a pattern, and the one doing the reading doesn't count it as theirs.
cells.act: cut through the story to what actually follows
cells.ask: Catch the story you're about to tell about what the other wants, and set it down. Look at just what they said, what happened, nothing added. Do it even once.
cells.core:
You read people. You see how it fits — the pattern with this one, what will work, where it goes — and the reading is smooth enough that it feels like the situation describing itself. Calculating takes no effort and draws no credit. The mechanism is in your hands, and you don't call it that.

So for once, cut through the story. Where you'd smooth the exchange with a read on the other person, set that down and say the plain line instead — what you actually want from them — no calculation running underneath. It stays your choice whether to do it. The only thing that changes is that you can see the pattern, and the pattern sees you back.
cells.sheetLine: You read the room. The reading is yours.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that many possibilities are actually presenting themselves — the record says they gather to the heart, not that others have offered any. A reader could say the options never came from outside at all, which is why too much and too little read as one closed motion. The asks survive that: both are one move made on your own, no offer needed. The sentence serving the writer is the sweep about everything the heart might want.
